title: Injuries following accidents involving electric bicycles and conventional bicycles
summary:
Background:
Electric bicycles have become a popular means of transportation in recent years. While police statistics provide reliable data on the causes of accidents, information on injury types, injury severity, and treatments can only be systematically assessed in a clinical setting. The aim of this study is therefore to use existing data (retrospectively) to gain more detailed insights into injury severity following electric bicycle accidents compared to conventional bicycle accidents. In addition, patients will be surveyed (prospectively) to collect information that is not usually documented in routine clinical care, such as helmet use, whether the accident was recorded by the police, the type of bicycle, and how it was used.

Research Question:
The main objective is to determine whether severe injuries (defined as an Injury Severity Score, ISS ≥ 16) occur more frequently in electric bicycle accidents than in accidents involving conventional bicycles. Furthermore, injury patterns, demographic characteristics, treatments, and potential risk factors for severe injuries will be examined.

Methods:
For the analysis, retrospective data from 250 electric bicycle riders and 750 conventional bicycle riders will be evaluated. In addition, approximately 300 injured individuals will be included in a prospective survey. The association between bicycle type and severe injuries will be analyzed statistically, adjusting for age. Further research questions will be explored descriptively based on the collected patient data.
conditions: Injuries treated in the emergency department following accidents involving an electric bicycle (pedelec, S-pedelec, e-bike) or a bicycle without electric assistance.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
– Accident involving an electric bicycle (pedelec, S-pedelec, e-bike) or a bicycle without electric assistance
– Accident occurring within the defined study period (01/01/2019 – 12/31/2026)
– Patients of all ages
Exclusion criteria:
No involvement of an electric bicycle or a conventional bicycle in the accident.
